title: Cardinal Billing Account Endorsement-Fee Offset on Additional-Premium Bills: Questions Answered
content:
**Rule.** An endorsement-fee offset is subtracted from the relieved billing charge of a Cardinal Billing Account additional-premium bill: **$1.50** when the endorsement fees posted to the account less than one whole month before the bill date total at least $10.00, **$0.75** when they total more than zero but under $10.00, and none when no endorsement fee was posted in that window; the billing charge never goes below zero.

## Questions answered

**Which fees count?**
Endorsement fees charged to the account, as shown by the endorsement fee entries on its billing history, posted less than one whole month before the bill date, counted on calendar months. Other fees (late fees, installment fees, policy fees) do not count.

**Is the offset a percentage?**
No. It is a fixed amount of $1.50 or $0.75, subtracted from the billing charge after the relief rate has been applied to it.

**What if the offset is larger than the billing charge?**
The billing charge never goes below zero; it stops at $0.00.

| Endorsement fees posted in the window, in total | Offset |
|---|---|
| $10.00 or more | $1.50 |
| More than $0.00, under $10.00 | $0.75 |
| None posted | None |

**Hypothetical figures.** Endorsement fees of $10.00 in the window and a relieved billing charge of $2.00: $2.00 less $1.50, that is $0.50. Endorsement fees of $9.99 and a relieved billing charge of $0.60: $0.60 less $0.75 would fall below zero, so the billing charge is $0.00.
